I added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`. It returns the logins of users created in the last 7 days, newest first, and only admins can call it. I didn't run the build or any tests.

- **Repository:** `UserRepository.findLoginsCreatedSince(Instant)` is a JPQL query that returns just the login strings, in `UserRepository.java`.
- **Service:** `UserService.getRecentlyCreatedLogins()` works out the cutoff with `Instant.now(clock).minus(7, ChronoUnit.DAYS)`. It follows the project rule of injecting a `Clock`, so I added a `Clock` constructor parameter to `UserService`.
- **Clock bean:** The project had no `Clock` bean, so I added `config/ClockConfiguration.java` exposing `Clock.systemUTC()`.
- **Endpoint:** `UserResource.getRecentlyCreatedUsers()` is guarded with `AuthoritiesConstants.ADMIN`, as the other admin endpoints are. I placed it above `/users/{login}`, and Spring prefers the literal path over the `{login}` pattern, so the two don't clash.

I found no code in the repo that calls `new UserService(...)` directly, so the new constructor parameter shouldn't break existing code. Existing tests that mock the service's dependencies are worth a look once you build.

I didn't update the `notes/` folder, because the repo has no `notes/index.md` yet.
